q: Sodium reacts with water: Na(s) + H₂O(l) → NaOH(aq) + H₂(g). What are the numbers in front of Na, H₂O, NaOH and H₂ in the balanced equation?
explain: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂ has 2 Na, 4 H and 2 O on each side.

q: How many oxygen atoms are shown in 2Mg(NO₃)₂?
explain: Each Mg(NO₃)₂ has 2 × 3 = 6 oxygen atoms. Two of them have 2 × 6 = 12.

q: What is the relative formula mass, Mr, of hydrated copper(II) sulfate, CuSO₄·5H₂O? (Ar: H = 1, O = 16, S = 32, Cu = 64)
How many moles of solute are in 25.0 cm³ of a solution of concentration 0.20 mol/dm³?
explain: Moles = concentration × volume in dm³ = 0.20 × 0.0250 = 0.0050 mol.

q: Heating 124 g of copper(II) carbonate forms 80 g of copper(II) oxide. What mass of copper(II) oxide forms from 12.4 g of copper(II) carbonate?
explain: 12.4 g is one tenth of 124 g, so the mass of copper(II) oxide is one tenth of 80 g, which is 8.0 g.

q: Which word equation is correct for calcium carbonate reacting with dilute hydrochloric acid?
options: calcium carbonate + hydrochloric acid → calcium chloride + hydrogen
calcium carbonate + hydrochloric acid → calcium oxide + carbon dioxide
calcium carbonate + hydrochloric acid → calcium chloride + water + carbon dioxide
calcium carbonate + hydrochloric acid → calcium chloride + water
explain: Acids react with carbonates to give a salt, water and carbon dioxide.

q: Which row is correct? (Ar: H = 1, C = 12, O = 16; Avogadro constant = 6.02 × 10²³ per mol)
explain: 22 g ÷ 44 g/mol = 0.50 mol, and 0.50 × 6.02 × 10²³ = 3.01 × 10²³. The other rows have the wrong number of particles for the amount shown.

q: In a titration, 25.0 cm³ of hydrochloric acid is exactly neutralised by 20.0 cm³ of 0.125 mol/dm³ sodium hydroxide (HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O). What is the concentration of the acid in g/dm³? (Ar: H = 1, Cl = 35.5)
explain: Moles of NaOH = 0.125 × 0.0200 = 0.00250 mol = moles of HCl. Concentration = 0.00250 ÷ 0.0250 = 0.100 mol/dm³, and 0.100 × 36.5 = 3.65 g/dm³.

q: 1.50 g of impure zinc reacts with excess acid to give 360 cm³ of hydrogen at r.t.p. Assume the impurities do not react. What is the percentage purity of the zinc? (Ar: Zn = 65; molar gas volume = 24 dm³)
What is the relative formula mass, Mr, of calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂? (Ar: H = 1, O = 16, Ca = 40)
explain: Mr = 40 + 2 × (16 + 1) = 40 + 34 = 74. The bracket means two OH groups.

q: Which compound contains three different elements?
explain: NaOH contains sodium, oxygen and hydrogen. The other three each contain two elements.

q: Which equation for the burning of methane is correctly balanced?
explain: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O has 1 C, 4 H and 4 O on each side. The other equations are unbalanced in oxygen or hydrogen.

q: A model of a molecule shows one sulfur atom joined to two oxygen atoms. What is its formula?
explain: One S atom and two O atoms give SO₂, sulfur dioxide.

q: A solution of sodium hydroxide has a concentration of 40 g/dm³. What mass of sodium hydroxide is in 0.5 dm³ of this solution?
explain: Mass = concentration × volume = 40 g/dm³ × 0.5 dm³ = 20 g.

q: Aqueous sodium carbonate reacts with dilute sulfuric acid to form aqueous sodium sulfate, water and carbon dioxide gas. Which is the balanced equation with state symbols?
explain: The formulae Na₂CO₃ and Na₂SO₄ are needed to balance the charges, and the equation is already balanced with 1 H₂O. Sodium carbonate is aqueous and carbon dioxide is a gas.

q: How many molecules are there in 0.50 mol of water? (Avogadro constant = 6.02 × 10²³ per mol)
explain: Number of molecules = 0.50 × 6.02 × 10²³ = 3.01 × 10²³.

q: CaCO₃(s) + 2HCl(aq) → CaCl₂(aq) + H₂O(l) + CO₂(g). Excess acid is added to 5.0 g of calcium carbonate. What volume of carbon dioxide forms at r.t.p.? (Ar: C = 12, O = 16, Ca = 40; molar gas volume = 24 dm³)
explain: Mr of CaCO₃ = 100, so 5.0 g = 0.050 mol. The ratio CaCO₃ : CO₂ is 1 : 1, so volume = 0.050 × 24 = 1.2 dm³.

q: What is the relative formula mass, Mr, of hydrated sodium carbonate, Na₂CO₃·10H₂O? (Ar: H = 1, C = 12, O = 16, Na = 23)
How many different elements are present in ammonium sulfate, (NH₄)₂SO₄?
explain: The elements are nitrogen, hydrogen, sulfur and oxygen: 4 different elements.

q: Mg(s) + 2HCl(aq) → MgCl₂(aq) + H₂(g). What volume of 2.0 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid reacts exactly with 2.4 g of magnesium? (Ar: Mg = 24)
explain: Moles of Mg = 2.4 ÷ 24 = 0.10 mol, so HCl needed = 0.20 mol. Volume = 0.20 ÷ 2.0 = 0.10 dm³ = 100 cm³.

q: Which ionic equation represents the neutralisation of an acid by an alkali?
explain: Hydrogen ions from the acid react with hydroxide ions from the alkali to form water.

q: Which row gives the correct name and formula?
explain: Sodium hydroxide is NaOH. The others should be Ca(OH)₂, K₂CO₃ and Mg(NO₃)₂.

q: The chloride XCl₂ has a relative formula mass of 95. What is the relative atomic mass of X? (Ar: Cl = 35.5)
explain: 2 Cl = 71, so X = 95 − 71 = 24 (magnesium).

q: Which word equation correctly shows zinc reacting with dilute hydrochloric acid?
options: zinc + hydrochloric acid → zinc chloride + hydrogen
zinc + hydrochloric acid → zinc chloride + water
zinc + hydrochloric acid → zinc oxide + hydrogen chloride
zinc + hydrochloric acid → zinc hydroxide + hydrogen
explain: A metal reacting with a dilute acid forms a salt and hydrogen gas. The salt from hydrochloric acid is a chloride.

q: 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(l). What volume of oxygen reacts completely with 48 dm³ of hydrogen at r.t.p.?
explain: The ratio H₂ : O₂ is 2 : 1, so the oxygen volume is half of 48 dm³ = 24 dm³.

q: 12.8 g of copper reacts with oxygen to form 14.4 g of an oxide. What is the empirical formula of the oxide? (Ar: O = 16, Cu = 64)
explain: Mass of oxygen = 14.4 − 12.8 = 1.6 g. Moles: Cu = 12.8 ÷ 64 = 0.20; O = 1.6 ÷ 16 = 0.10. The ratio is 2 : 1, so Cu₂O.

q: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O. What mass of water forms when 8.0 g of methane burns completely? (Ar: H = 1, C = 12, O = 16)
explain: 8.0 g ÷ 16 g/mol = 0.50 mol of CH₄. The ratio CH₄ : H₂O is 1 : 2, so 1.0 mol of H₂O = 18 g.

q: Which sample contains the largest number of molecules? (Ar: H = 1, C = 12, N = 14, O = 16)
explain: 4 g of H₂ is 2 mol. 32 g of O₂, 44 g of CO₂ and 17 g of NH₃ are each 1 mol.

q: What is the relative formula mass, Mr, of magnesium nitrate, Mg(NO₃)₂? (Ar: N = 14, O = 16, Mg = 24)
0.10 mol of a solute is dissolved in water to make 250 cm³ of solution. What is the concentration in mol/dm³?
explain: 250 cm³ = 0.250 dm³. Concentration = moles ÷ volume = 0.10 ÷ 0.250 = 0.40 mol/dm³.
